newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 to $10 a tonne higher on Tuesday, as traders expected speculators to follow-through on Monday's steep run-up.

New York cocoa futures jumped sharply on Monday, as speculators, led by commodity funds, propelled the market to new eight-yer highs. September cocoa shot-up $83 a tonne, to $1,696, after ranging between a new life-of-contract high of $1,699 and $1,616.

Spot July leapt $97, to close at a fresh contract high of $1,663, the highest nearby level on the continuous weekly charts since 1989. The back months -- which also set lifetime highs -- rose $72 to $80.
Technically, strong resistance in the September contract was pegged near $1,732, with a long-term chart objective seen at $1,817, traders said.
After Monday's close, the CSCE said it will raise margins on all cocoa contracts by $200 to $800, effective today.
In London, cocoa futures rallied to one-year highs early Tuesday, bolstered by keen speculative buying. LIFFE September was up 21 stg at the midday break, to 1,151 stg, after peaking at 1,160 stg.
